title: A Monsoon for the Passage
premise: Jude Fairweather, a surveyor for a decommissioned colonial-era rail network, pulls a sealed chest from a flooded riverbed and finds inside it the records of an expedition that vanished in 1947 carrying proof of a border that would redraw three nations. The chest's seal belongs to a country that no longer exists, and both a descendant of the expedition's lost cartographer and a government archivist who wants the chest buried forever begin closing in on her. As Jude follows the dead expedition's route upriver during monsoon season, she discovers her own grandfather was its engineer—and that the map of closed lines she inherited is the other half of theirs. In the end, Jude must choose between returning the chest to the river to protect the living, or bringing it home to give the dead their names back; she chooses memory, publishing the route under every lost expedition member's name, including her grandfather's, and finally measures her own life in years instead of miles.
about_author: D. M. Lockridge is the pen name of a former hydrographic surveyor who spent a decade mapping rivers across Southeast Asia before turning to fiction. They write adventure novels about people whose professions keep them at one remove from their own lives.

chapters.title: The Gauge of Quiet Years
chapters.summary: Jude Fairweather surveys a shuttered mountain rail line, measuring decay with the detachment of someone who has stopped counting birthdays. A letter from a solicitor about her late grandfather's estate goes unopened. POV: Jude. Beat: establish her self-imposed invisibility and the ache beneath it.

chapters.title: What the River Keeps
chapters.summary: After a landslide diverts the river, Jude wades into exposed silt to check a bridge footing and finds a brass-bound chest stamped with a seal she doesn't recognize—a nation that vanished from maps in 1948. POV: Jude. Beat: wonder curdling into unease as she realizes what she's holding.

chapters.title: A Dead Country's Signature
chapters.summary: In her rail shed, Jude opens the chest: expedition logs, photographs, and half a survey map ending mid-route. The last entry names an engineer—E. Fairweather. Her hands shake. POV: Jude. Beat: the personal hook lands; inheritance becomes literal.

chapters.title: The Man Who Counts Other People's Papers
chapters.summary: Archivist Elias Voss arrives in town asking quiet questions about river salvage, claiming academic interest. Jude lies smoothly and hates how easily it comes. POV: Voss. Beat: introduce the antagonist's charm and his institutional mandate to bury the past.

chapters.title: Half a Map
chapters.summary: Jude overlays the expedition map on her own charts of closed lines and realizes they interlock—the routes were drawn by the same hand, decades apart. Her grandfather didn't just join the expedition; he finished its work alone. POV: Jude. Beat: revelation that reframes her inheritance.

chapters.title: The Cartographer's Granddaughter
chapters.summary: Mara Osei arrives from abroad tracing her grandmother, the expedition's cartographer who never came home. She recognizes the chest's seal instantly and offers Jude partnership—or surveillance, Jude can't tell. POV: Mara. Beat: alliance formed on mutual need and mutual suspicion.

chapters.title: Monsoon Warning
chapters.summary: Voss files paperwork declaring the chest state property; Jude has forty-eight hours before seizure. She and Mara load a boat with supplies and the chest, slipping downriver ahead of the storm season's first wall of rain. POV: Jude. Beat: point of no return; the journey begins.

chapters.title: Closed Lines
chapters.summary: Following the dead expedition's route upriver, Jude reads her grandfather's margin notes like letters to her. Mara shares her grandmother's smuggled letters, and the two women compare inheritances neither asked for. POV: Mara. Beat: deepening trust; grief shared becomes bearable.

chapters.title: The First Camp
chapters.summary: They find the expedition's first camp preserved in mud: ration tins, a child's shoe no log explains, and scratch marks inside a tent flap counting days past the official end date. Someone survived longer than history recorded. POV: Jude. Beat: dread rises; the story behind the documents darkens.

chapters.title: Voss on the Water
chapters.summary: Voss charters his own boat with two 'porters' who carry rifles badly concealed. He sends Jude a radio message offering her grandfather's full service record in exchange for the chest—an offer designed to make her complicit. POV: Voss. Beat: antagonist tightens the screws; temptation made personal.

chapters.title: Rapids and Reckoning
chapters.summary: A monsoon surge nearly swamps them in a gorge; Jude's engineering saves the boat but the chest takes water, and ink begins to bleed from pages seventy years dry. To save the documents she'll have to open the sealed inner compartment. POV: Jude. Beat: crisis forces escalation; stakes become irreversible.

chapters.title: The Compartment
chapters.summary: Inside the compartment: the completed border survey, and a signed order proving the expedition wasn't lost—it was abandoned deliberately, its members written off to bury the map. E. Fairweather's signature is on the protest against it. POV: Mara. Beat: the central secret surfaces; anger replaces mystery.

chapters.title: The Village That Remembers
chapters.summary: A riverside village still keeps a shrine to 'the map people' who died nearby. An elder recognizes Mara's family name and gives her grandmother's field notebook, kept sacred for three generations. POV: Mara. Beat: emotional peak of connection; the dead are not gone where memory lives.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Confluence
chapters.summary: One of Mara's hired guides sells their position to Voss. At the confluence, the porters take the chest at gunpoint—but Jude has already split the documents, hiding the border survey in her surveying instruments. POV: Jude. Beat: betrayal and loss; the chase turns desperate.

chapters.title: Running the Closed Line
chapters.summary: Jude and Mara flee down a rail tunnel her grandfather mapped, using a handcar on rotted track while Voss's men close in. The tunnel floods behind them. They emerge downstream, exhausted, with half the truth and no boat. POV: Jude. Beat: pure momentum; survival by inheritance of skill.

chapters.title: What Voss Wants Buried
chapters.summary: Captured briefly and released without the chest's remaining contents, Jude realizes Voss isn't protecting a government—he's protecting his own grandfather, the officer who signed the abandonment order. Two legacies, mirror images. POV: Voss. Beat: humanize the antagonist; his motive becomes tragic.

chapters.title: The Last Survey Marker
chapters.summary: At the route's terminus, they find her grandfather's final camp and his unfinished letter: he spent his life unable to decide whether the map should surface, and left the choice to whoever found his work. Jude understands her whole inheritance at last. POV: Jude. Beat: thematic climax; the choice is handed to her.

chapters.title: High Water
chapters.summary: Voss corners them at the river crossing as the monsoon peaks. Jude offers him a trade: the original documents for his grandfather's confession, published alongside hers. He refuses—and then the river decides, taking the chest and nearly taking him. Jude saves him. POV: Jude. Beat: climax; mercy over vengeance, nature as final arbiter.

chapters.title: Salvage
chapters.summary: The chest is gone, but Jude's hidden duplicate survives, water-stained and legible enough. Mara verifies the cartography against her grandmother's notebook. What remains is enough—not for courts, but for memory. POV: Mara. Beat: quiet aftermath; deciding what the truth is for.

chapters.title: Names Read Aloud
chapters.summary: In the village shrine, Jude and Mara read the eleven expedition members' names aloud and add them to the record, publishing the full account with every signature attached—including the confession Voss finally provides anonymously. POV: Jude. Beat: resolution of the external plot; the dead receive their names.

chapters.title: Miles Versus Years
chapters.summary: Jude returns to the rail line one last time, not to measure it but to walk it. She opens her grandfather's estate letter at last and finds only a photograph of the expedition, young faces smiling, and one line: 'Finish it or forgive it.' She has done both. POV: Jude. Beat: personal resolution; identity reclaimed.

chapters.title: A Monsoon for the Passage
chapters.summary: Months later, Jude takes a contract surveying a living railway, and Mara writes from abroad that a memorial stands at the village shrine. Rain falls on new track. Jude counts the years since the river gave up its chest, and lets herself count forward too. POV: Jude. Beat: coda; the passage complete, life measured in time again.
